name: Notstrom, a rough first version for the look and feel test
format: AAC (.m4a), stereo, 96 kbit/s (the menu theme: 128 kbit/s); an MP3 would leave a gap at the seam of the loop
note: One loop of 8 bars (26.667 s) in four layers that start together and loop in sync. A layer file is stored 6 dB down. The gains of a level set the loudness: about -34, -32, -30 and -27 dB (mean power, `npm run render-mix`), which keeps the music well under the voices and effects. The levels are cut by the game on the next bar line. See archive/audio-source/music/README.md for where the layers come from.

effects.what: the ship leaves the hyperspace (the ring is at 0.1 to 0.25 s of the film, the ship flies from 0.33 s to 2.6 s): an underwater rocket or submarine, 5.85 s; louder (+5 dB, baked in per sample without a limiter; the file is 4.6 dB lower and the gain 1.5. The ffmpeg `volume` filter with `eval=frame` changes its gain in steps per frame, which crackled) from 2.4 s, where the visor with the reflection begins (2.7 s), its natural peak falls there; fades out from 4.5 s

the visor (2.7 s to 6.3 s of the film; it starts a little before): Tilly breathing, very light, slowed to 85 % by resampling (a little lower in pitch, no time-stretch artefacts) and muffled as in a helmet (low-passed at 1.2 and 1.8 kHz): an exhale and an inhale, a pause of 0.2 s, the same two again (take A of call 48, 3.8 s to 5.6 s of the take: the spoken Hhh anchors at 0.3 s and 2.8 s crackle and are left out)
